SR-CON-001.text: | SR-CON-001 | **Self-contained:** the default distribution MUST run with zero external network dependencies (no SaaS, no cloud API, no phone-home, no CDN assets, no package fetch at runtime). | P0 |

SR-CON-002.text: | SR-CON-002 | **Local-first:** all processing, storage, indexing, embedding, inference and UI serving happen inside the customer-controlled boundary by default; the system MUST function fully offline. | P0 |

SR-CON-003.text: | SR-CON-003 | **No egress by default:** outbound traffic MUST be denied by default via network policy and application-level egress gateway; any permitted egress is allowlisted, logged and attributable. | P0 |

SR-CON-004.text: | SR-CON-004 | **Everything configurable, safely:** every behavior in this document that says "configurable" MUST be a typed, versioned, validated, auditable setting with a safe default (§12.3). | P0 |

SR-CON-005.text: | SR-CON-005 | **LLM-optional:** ingestion, graph construction, validation, deterministic query, impact analysis, lineage and reporting MUST work with no LLM present. | P0 |
| SR-ING-042 | **Traversal-first retrieval** (no embeddings required) is the baseline retrieval mode; embeddings enhance recall but are never prerequisite (consistent with SR-CON-005). | P0 |

SR-CON-006.text: | SR-CON-006 | **Evidence-first:** every returned fact carries source, method (asserted/derived/inferred/curated), confidence, freshness and policy-filter notice. | P0 |

SR-CON-007.text: | SR-CON-007 | **Clean-room and license-clean:** study external products and papers for ideas only; produce an independent implementation, SBOM and license report per release. | P0 |

SR-CON-008.text: | SR-CON-008 | **Adapters over lock-in:** no component outside an adapter may import a vendor-specific graph, vector, model, bus or storage SDK. Enforced by architecture tests. | P0 |

SR-CON-009.text: | SR-CON-009 | **Vendor-neutral data ownership:** customers can export all data, ontology, config and audit trails in open formats at any time (§7.9). | P0 |

SR-CON-010.text: | SR-CON-010 | Cloud capabilities MUST be delivered as **Service Provider plugins** (e.g., object storage, managed graph DB, managed search, KMS/HSM, IdP, queue, LLM endpoint, monitoring sink) selectable per capability, per tenant. | P0 |

SR-CON-011.text: | SR-CON-011 | Every plugin MUST ship a **Data-Flow Manifest** declaring data classes sent/received, destinations, regions, retention and whether data can leave the tenant boundary. Installation MUST display it and require admin approval; the egress gateway enforces it at runtime. | P0 |

SR-CON-012.text: | SR-CON-012 | Provide reference adapters for the three hyperscalers' object storage, KMS, identity federation and managed graph/search where available (e.g., Amazon Neptune/OpenSearch/S3/KMS, Azure Blob/Key Vault/Entra ID/Cosmos Gremlin, GCP GCS/KMS/Cloud Identity). | P1 |

SR-CON-014.text: | SR-CON-014 | A tenant MUST be able to switch a capability between local and cloud providers via migration tooling (e.g., local object store → cloud bucket) with verification and rollback. | P2 |

SR-ARC-001.text: | SR-ARC-001 | **Modular monolith first, service-extractable:** modules communicate through typed interfaces/events and MUST be separable into independently scalable services without code rewrite (preserves the prior `NFR-MAINT-001` boundary). | P0 |

SR-ARC-002.text: | SR-ARC-002 | **Ports-and-adapters:** Graph Store, Vector Store, Search, Object Store, Relational Store, Event Bus, Model Provider, Identity Provider, Secret/KMS, Scheduler and Notification are ports with versioned contracts and a conformance test kit. | P0 |

SR-ARC-003.text: | SR-ARC-003 | **Event backbone:** an append-only event log (pluggable: embedded log for DP-0; NATS JetStream/Kafka-class for clustered) carries ingestion, mutation, policy and audit events; consumers are idempotent (outbox pattern). | P0 |

SR-ARC-004.text: | SR-ARC-004 | **Single canonical contract per concept:** one versioned schema registry for entities, edges, events, QueryPlan, agent contract, config and plugin manifest; all APIs and UIs derive from it (generated, not hand-copied). | P0 |

SR-ARC-005.text: | SR-ARC-005 | **Distributed by design:** stateless API/query/worker tiers scale horizontally; stateful tiers (graph, vector, search, relational, object, log) support replication and partitioning per backend capability. | P0 |

SR-ARC-006.text: | SR-ARC-006 | **Consistency model documented and tested:** strong consistency within a graph partition for writes and read-your-writes for the writer; eventual consistency for derived indexes (vector, search, materialized views) with measurable lag SLOs and a staleness indicator surfaced to users. | P0 |

SR-ARC-007.text: | SR-ARC-007 | **Exactly-once effects** via idempotency keys, deterministic IDs and replay-safe mutations; at-least-once delivery acceptable at transport level. | P0 |

SR-ARC-008.text: | SR-ARC-008 | **Hybrid logical clocks / bitemporal fields** on all mutations (valid time, transaction time) so federated and replayed data order deterministically. | P1 |

SR-ARC-009.text: | SR-ARC-009 | **Federation:** queries MAY span multiple graph backends and multiple sites (hub-and-spoke or mesh) with partial-result semantics, per-site policy enforcement and no raw-data movement unless permitted. | P2 |

SR-ARC-011.text: | SR-ARC-011 | **Architecture fitness tests** in CI: forbidden imports, layering rules, adapter-only vendor SDK usage, no hand-maintained inventories, no cross-tenant code paths without tenant context. | P0 |

SR-ARC-012.text: | SR-ARC-012 | **Mandatory ADR process:** every decision that changes a port, a default component or a supported-backend tier needs an ADR with alternatives, license review and benchmark evidence. | P0 |

SR-GDB-001.text: | SR-GDB-001 | All graph access MUST go through the **Graph Store Port** exposing: schema ops, bulk load, transactional upsert (idempotent by canonical ID), traversal, path, neighborhood, aggregation, full-scan with cursor, index management, snapshot/export, health and statistics. | P0 |
| FR-GRAPH (store, domains, schema, IDs, meta-graph, bridges, Gremlin repo, indexes, journal, RDF/OWL, multi-backend) | §5, §7.5, SR-GDB-001…010 |

SR-GDB-002.text: | SR-GDB-002 | Each adapter MUST publish a **Capability Manifest** (example in §5.6). The planner uses it to choose pushdown vs in-engine execution and to refuse or degrade unsupported plans *explicitly* (never silently). | P0 |

SR-GDB-003.text: | SR-GDB-003 | A **backend-neutral conformance suite** (contract tests + golden queries + performance probes + failure injection) MUST gate every adapter. Backend-specific behavior (e.g., HugeGraph 1.7 not honoring UNIQUE edge indexes, requiring SECONDARY + sort-key emulation) is recorded in the manifest, not scattered in code. | P0 |

SR-GDB-004.text: | SR-GDB-004 | **Certification tiers:** Tier A *Certified* (full conformance, benchmarked, HA validated, supported under SLA); Tier B *Compatible* (documented capability gaps); Tier C *Community/Experimental*. Marketing MUST NOT claim support beyond the tier. | P0 |

SR-GDB-005.text: | SR-GDB-005 | **Polyglot persistence:** each logical graph domain (e.g., org, code, incident, lineage, meta) MAY bind to a different backend and tier (hot/warm/cold); cross-domain **bridge edges** are resolved by the federation layer. | P1 |

SR-GDB-006.text: | SR-GDB-006 | **Online migration** between backends (export → verify counts/checksums/golden queries → dual-write or cutover → rollback) MUST be supported for Tier A pairs. | P1 |
| RK-15 | Upstream project changes (relicensing, abandonment, e.g., an embedded engine's maintenance status) | Adapter isolation, exit paths, migration tooling (SR-GDB-006) |

SR-GDB-007.text: | SR-GDB-007 | **Virtual/zero-ETL graph mode:** optionally expose existing relational/lakehouse data as a graph view through declarative mappings (OBDA/virtual-graph style) without copying data. | P2 |
| Virtual graph engines over SQL/lakehouse (e.g., PuppyGraph-style, Ontop-style OBDA) | openCypher/Gremlin/SPARQL | Yes | Some | P2 | Zero-ETL mode (SR-GDB-007) |

SR-GDB-008.text: | SR-GDB-008 | **Multi-model graph support:** property graph (LPG) and RDF are both first-class; RDF-star/reification patterns and LPG↔RDF round-trip mappings MUST be defined and tested. | P1 |

SR-GDB-009.text: | SR-GDB-009 | **Graph versioning:** every mutation produces an `EntityRevision`; point-in-time ("as-of") reads and diffs between revisions MUST be supported (full snapshot/diff at P1). | P1 |

SR-GDB-010.text: | SR-GDB-010 | **Embedded engine option** for DP-0/edge nodes with no server process, and an in-memory engine for tests only (selection is explicit configuration, never a silent fallback). | P0 |

SR-GDB-011.text: | SR-GDB-011 | **Relational metadata/config store:** PostgreSQL as the clustered default, SQLite for single-node DP-0; ports allow customer-standard engines (SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL/MariaDB) at P2. | P0 |

SR-GDB-012.text: | SR-GDB-012 | **Object/raw store:** filesystem (DP-0), S3-compatible (clustered), and cloud blob adapters. Raw captures are immutable, content-addressed (SHA-256), encrypted, and retention-managed. | P0 |

SR-GDB-013.text: | SR-GDB-013 | **Event bus adapters:** embedded log, NATS JetStream-class, Kafka/Redpanda-class, RabbitMQ, cloud queues. | P0/P1 |

SR-GDB-014.text: | SR-GDB-014 | **Cache:** in-process plus a Redis-protocol-compatible adapter; every cache key MUST include tenant, policy-version and graph-revision. | P0 |

SR-GDB-015.text: | SR-GDB-015 | **Durable workflow engine** built in (retry, timers, human-approval steps, sagas); optional adapters for Temporal/Airflow/Dagster/Prefect-class orchestrators. | P1 |

SR-GDB-016.text: | SR-GDB-016 | **Component license matrix:** every bundled and optional component is classified (permissive / weak copyleft / strong copyleft or network-copyleft / source-available / commercial). Anything other than permissive MUST NOT be bundled without legal sign-off and MUST be offered as bring-your-own where needed. | P0 |

| RK-02 | License contamination (copyleft, network-copyleft, source-available, commercial-only components bundled in a sold product) | License matrix (SR-GDB-016), bring-your-own mode, legal gate in CI, clean-room rule |

SR-VDB-001.text: | SR-VDB-001 | **Vector Store Port:** upsert/delete by ID with metadata, filtered kNN, hybrid (dense + sparse/BM25), namespace-per-tenant, snapshot/restore, index rebuild, embedding-model version tracking. | P0 |

SR-VDB-002.text: | SR-VDB-002 | **Adapters:** embedded (FAISS/hnswlib/USearch/LanceDB-class), PostgreSQL pgvector, Qdrant, Milvus, Weaviate, Chroma, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch k-NN, Redis-compatible vector, Vespa, graph-native vector indexes (e.g., Neo4j), plus cloud-managed (Pinecone, Azure AI Search, Vertex AI Vector Search, Atlas Vector Search) under DP-3/4 only. | P0 (embedded, pgvector) / P1 (rest) |

SR-VDB-003.text: | SR-VDB-003 | **Index strategies configurable:** HNSW, IVF-PQ, DiskANN-class disk indexes, scalar/product/binary quantization, filtered-search strategies, per-collection recall/latency targets. | P1 |

SR-VDB-004.text: | SR-VDB-004 | **Multi-vector and multimodal:** text, code, table, image, audio-transcript, and node/graph embeddings; late-interaction (ColBERT-style) and sparse-learned (SPLADE-style) as optional retrievers. | P2 |

SR-VDB-005.text: | SR-VDB-005 | **Embedding governance:** embeddings are derived data; they inherit the classification and access policy of their source, are deleted when the source is erased (§14.3), and are re-generated on model change with versioned side-by-side indexes and cut-over. | P0 |
| SR-LLM-007 | **Embedding service** with model versioning, batch/online modes, multilingual and code models, and re-embedding jobs (SR-VDB-005). | P0 |

SR-VDB-006.text: | SR-VDB-006 | **Full-text/search port:** BM25 keyword, phrase, fuzzy, facets, highlighting, multilingual analyzers; adapters for embedded engine (Tantivy/SQLite-FTS class), PostgreSQL FTS, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch class. | P0 |

SR-VDB-007.text: | SR-VDB-007 | A deployment with **no vector store** MUST still pass the core NL acceptance suite using graph + full-text retrieval (degraded semantic recall is acceptable and MUST be signalled). | P0 |
| FR-RAG (router, GraphRAG, local models, no mandatory vector DB, eval, adaptive) | §9.2, SR-VDB-007, SR-LLM |

SR-QRY-001.text: | SR-QRY-001 | The compiler MUST accept EOQL, Gremlin, openCypher, GQL (subset first), SPARQL, SQL (analytics) and NL-produced plans, validate them against the ontology and the caller's policy, and lower them per the Capability Manifest. | P0 |

SR-QRY-002.text: | SR-QRY-002 | **Never execute raw model- or user-generated graph queries** without schema-aware validation, policy rewrite, depth/timeout/expansion/cost limits and expensive-pattern detection. Raw dialect access is an admin-gated, audited feature. | P0 |

SR-QRY-003.text: | SR-QRY-003 | **Query Explain:** every query returns (on request) the plan, chosen backend(s), pushdowns, estimated vs actual cost, and the generated dialect text. | P0 |

SR-QRY-004.text: | SR-QRY-004 | **Dialect round-trip tests:** a golden corpus (≥ 500 queries per Tier A backend, growing) MUST prove IR → dialect semantic equivalence by result comparison on shared fixtures. | P0 |
| Dialect equivalence | IR → dialect result equivalence on shared fixtures (SR-QRY-004) |

SR-QRY-005.text: | SR-QRY-005 | **Parameterization everywhere;** string-built queries are forbidden (injection defense). | P0 |

SR-QRY-006.text: | SR-QRY-006 | **Saved queries, query libraries, templates and versioned "question catalog"** per tenant/workspace, shareable and permission-aware. | P0 |

SR-QRY-008.text: | SR-QRY-008 | **Graph algorithm library** callable from plans (≥ 60 algorithms by P1): shortest/k-shortest/all-simple paths, reachability, SCC/WCC, topological order and cycle detection, dominators/critical path, PageRank/personalized PageRank, betweenness/closeness/degree/eigenvector centrality, community detection (Leiden/Louvain/label propagation), triangle/clustering/k-core, similarity (Jaccard/cosine/Adamic-Adar), node embeddings (node2vec/GraphSAGE-class), link prediction, motif matching,

SR-QRY-009.text: | SR-QRY-009 | **Incremental / precomputed accelerators:** transitive-closure or reachability indexes for impact queries, materialized views per persona, summary edges, and top-k caches, all invalidated by graph-revision events. | P1 |

SR-QRY-010.text: | SR-QRY-010 | **Federated query** across backends and sites with per-source policy enforcement and partial results. | P2 |

SR-QRY-011.text: | SR-QRY-011 | **Time travel:** `AS OF`, `BETWEEN`, `DIFF` over revisions for every query class where backends or the revision store allow. | P1 |

SR-QRY-012.text: | SR-QRY-012 | **Multilingual query front-ends** (NL, EOQL) with locale-aware date/number handling. | P1 |

SR-ING-001.text: | SR-ING-001 | **Connector SDK** (Python and TypeScript at P0; Go/Java at P1) with a stable contract: `discover`, `authenticate`, `fetch(cursor)`, `schema`, `health`, `metrics`, `capabilities`, `deletion_semantics`; connectors run sandboxed with declared scopes. | P0 |

SR-ING-003.text: | SR-ING-003 | **Change capture:** polling, webhooks, CDC (log-based where the source supports it), file watchers, stream consumers; deletes handled by tombstones with configurable semantics (soft delete, retire edge, hard delete on policy). | P0 |

SR-ING-004.text: | SR-ING-004 | **Credential isolation:** connector secrets live only in the secret store, scoped per tenant/connector, rotated, never logged, never visible to plugins other than the owning connector. | P0 |

SR-ING-005.text: | SR-ING-005 | **Connector marketplace-ready packaging:** signed manifest, version, compatibility range, data-flow manifest, test fixtures, health contract. | P1 |

SR-ING-006.text: | SR-ING-006 | **Streaming and batch share one pipeline:** the same stages and mapping specs serve both; back-pressure and priority lanes per tenant. | P0 |

SR-ING-007.text: | SR-ING-007 | **Large-JSON handling:** streaming parse (never load whole file), gz/zstd/archive support, malformed-record quarantine with line/offset pointers, numeric precision and Unicode/timezone normalization, binary blob offload. | P0 |

SR-ING-010.text: | SR-ING-010 | The **Schema Profiler** MUST infer types, nullability, cardinality, uniqueness, enumerations, formats (email, UUID, URL, IP/CIDR, ISO date/time, currency, phone, IBAN, ARN/URN, git SHA, ticket keys like `ABC-123`, file paths), nesting shape, and drift across versions of a payload. | P0 |

SR-ING-011.text: | SR-ING-011 | **Entity detection:** record types from top-level arrays/envelopes/discriminator fields; nested objects classified as *embedded value*, *child entity*, or *reference* using a scored heuristic (key presence, size, reuse across parents, naming, user override). | P0 |

SR-ING-012.text: | SR-ING-012 | **Key detection:** natural/surrogate key candidates; composite keys; stability scoring across runs; canonical ID minting strategy per type (deterministic, namespaced, collision-safe). | P0 |

SR-ING-013.text: | SR-ING-013 | **Relationship discovery — explicit:** foreign-key-like fields, `$ref`/JSON Pointer, URLs to known entities, `*_id`/`parent`/`owner` conventions, join-table detection (junction → edge with properties), polymorphic `type`+`id` pairs, array-of-IDs, hierarchy via parent pointers or path strings. | P0 |

SR-ING-014.text: | SR-ING-014 | **Relationship discovery — statistical:** inclusion-dependency and value-overlap discovery across datasets (MinHash/LSH containment for scale), name and embedding-based schema matching, co-occurrence, temporal proximity, co-change coupling, mention extraction in text (entity linking). | P0 (value overlap) / P1 |

SR-ING-015.text: | SR-ING-015 | **Relationship discovery — operational:** service-call edges from traces/logs, config references (env var → secret → account), IaC dependency edges, build/runtime dependencies from SBOM and lockfiles, code call/import graphs (tree-sitter and SCIP/LSIF-class indexers), SQL lineage parsing, access-log derived usage edges. | P0 (engineering set) / P1 |
| FR-CODE (parser, Python/TS, commit-symbol, call/import edges) | SR-ING-015, §19 Software/IT pack |

SR-ING-016.text: | SR-ING-016 | **Edge classes and honesty:** every edge is `ASSERTED` (source says so), `DERIVED` (deterministic rule), `INFERRED` (statistical/ML/LLM), or `CURATED` (human-approved), with confidence and method. Inferred edges are excluded from "authoritative" answers unless the query opts in. *(Analogous to Graphify's EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS confidence tags, extended with CURATED and DERIVED.)* | P0 |

SR-ING-017.text: | SR-ING-017 | **Ontology induction:** propose classes, properties, relation types and hierarchies from data; present for steward approval in the Mapping Studio; support *ontology-first*, *data-first* and *hybrid* modes. | P1 |

SR-ING-018.text: | SR-ING-018 | **Link prediction / graph completion** (heuristic and learned, e.g., translational and GNN-class models) proposes missing edges into a review queue; auto-assertion only above a tenant-configured threshold. | P2 |

SR-ING-019.text: | SR-ING-019 | **Mapping DSL:** declarative, versioned, diff-able mappings (YAML/JSON) with RML/R2RML and JSON-LD `@context` import/export; generated by inference, editable by humans, testable on samples. | P0 |

SR-ING-020.text: | SR-ING-020 | **Schema drift handling:** new/changed/removed fields trigger drift events, auto-compatible mapping updates when safe, and steward review when not; mappings are pinned per run for reproducibility. | P0 |

SR-ING-030.text: | SR-ING-030 | Deterministic rules first (exact keys, normalized emails/IDs), then probabilistic (blocking via sorted-neighborhood/canopy/LSH; pairwise similarity with string/phonetic/numeric/date/embedding features; Fellegi–Sunter-class scoring and/or trained classifiers). | P0 |

SR-ING-031.text: | SR-ING-031 | **Collective resolution** using graph context (shared neighbors, co-authorship, same repo/team) and transitive clustering with constraints; **survivorship rules** produce golden records with per-attribute source precedence. | P1 |

SR-ING-032.text: | SR-ING-032 | Every merge is **explainable, reversible (unmerge), audited**; three bands (auto-merge / human review / reject) with tenant-set thresholds and an active-learning review queue. | P0 |

SR-ING-033.text: | SR-ING-033 | **Cross-source ID crosswalk** persisted as first-class graph structure (`SAME_AS` with confidence and evidence) so aliases resolve at query time. | P0 |

SR-ING-040.text: | SR-ING-040 | Derived graphs are computed **incrementally** from mutation events; full rebuild MUST be possible and verified equivalent to the incremental result. | P0 |

SR-ING-041.text: | SR-ING-041 | **Graphify-class artifacts:** auto-generate portable `graph.json`, interactive HTML, and a markdown/wiki report per graph or subgraph; support export to Obsidian/Markdown vaults; support post-commit/post-merge hooks and PR-impact triage (rank open change requests by graph impact; flag overlapping-community conflicts). | P1 |

SR-ING-042.text: | SR-ING-042 | **Traversal-first retrieval** (no embeddings required) is the baseline retrieval mode; embeddings enhance recall but are never prerequisite (consistent with SR-CON-005). | P0 |

SR-ING-043.text: | SR-ING-043 | **Pre-aggregation:** per-type degree/centrality, per-edge-class reachability, and domain-to-domain bridge statistics are maintained to answer overview and impact questions within latency targets. | P1 |

SR-ING-050.text: | SR-ING-050 | Validation rules with severities (`INFO/WARN/ERROR/BLOCKER`), remediation suggestions, quarantine with replay, and a data-quality scorecard (completeness, freshness, uniqueness, consistency, confidence distribution) per source and per domain. | P0 |

SR-ING-051.text: | SR-ING-051 | **Freshness SLOs** per connector with alerting and a user-visible "knowledge age" on every answer. | P0 |

SR-ING-052.text: | SR-ING-052 | **Idempotency tests:** re-running an ingestion produces zero net graph change; interrupted runs resume without duplicates (restart-safe). | P0 |
| FR-INGEST (raw capture, canonicalization, idempotency, lifecycle, DLQ) | §7.2, SR-ING-052 |

SR-ING-053.text: | SR-ING-053 | **Reconciliation reports** (source counts vs graph counts, orphan edges, dangling references) on schedule. | P0 |

SR-ING-070.text: | SR-ING-070 | Export formats: JSON/NDJSON, CSV, Parquet, GraphML, GEXF, GraphSON, openCypher bulk CSV, RDF (Turtle, N-Quads, JSON-LD, RDF-star), DOT/Mermaid, Markdown vault, interactive HTML; full-tenant export bundle (data + ontology + mappings + config + audit). | P0 |

SR-ONT-001.text: | SR-ONT-001 | **Ontology service** stores ontologies as versioned artifacts (semantic versioning, diff, migration plans, deprecation lifecycle). Every graph element pins `ontology_version`. | P0 |

SR-ONT-002.text: | SR-ONT-002 | **Import/export:** OWL 2 (RDF/XML, Turtle, Manchester), RDFS, SKOS, JSON Schema, JSON-LD contexts, LinkML-style schemas, Protégé project interop, CSV glossaries; export of the active ontology to OWL and SHACL shapes. | P0 |

SR-ONT-003.text: | SR-ONT-003 | **Ontology Studio** (UI): visual class/property editor, relationship canvas, constraint editor, glossary/taxonomy manager, mapping designer, diff/merge, impact preview ("what existing data breaks if I change this?"), review-and-approve workflow with roles. | P0 |

SR-ONT-005.text: | SR-ONT-005 | **Business glossary and taxonomy** (SKOS-compatible): terms, synonyms, multilingual labels, definitions, owners, approved-status; terms link to ontology concepts and to physical fields; NL layer uses the glossary for grounding. | P0 |

SR-ONT-007.text: | SR-ONT-007 | **Tenant-renamable terminology (white-label semantics):** a tenant may rename "Service" → "Application", "Incident" → "Case", etc., without changing the underlying canonical type. | P0 |

SR-ONT-008.text: | SR-ONT-008 | **Ontology-driven generation:** GraphQL schema, REST resources, form UIs, validation, and docs generated from the ontology. | P1 |

SR-ONT-009.text: | SR-ONT-009 | **Governed evolution:** proposals, review, approval, scheduled rollout, backward-compat checks, automatic data migration jobs, rollback. | P0 |

SR-ONT-020.text: | SR-ONT-020 | **Inference tiers:** (a) graph-native derivations (transitive, inverse, symmetric, property chains), (b) rule-based (Datalog/SWRL-class) materialization with provenance, (c) OWL-RL/EL profile reasoning where RDF back-ends support it, (d) probabilistic/ML inference proposals. Every inferred fact is labeled `DERIVED` or `INFERRED` and explainable ("why is this true?" returns the rule and premises). | P1 |

SR-ONT-021.text: | SR-ONT-021 | **Truth maintenance:** retraction of premises retracts conclusions; contradictions are surfaced as validation findings, never silently resolved. | P1 |

SR-ONT-022.text: | SR-ONT-022 | **Temporal and defeasible semantics** for roles/ownership that change over time (valid-time intervals on edges). | P1 |

SR-RAG-001.text: | SR-RAG-001 | **Router** chooses strategy per query class with a logged rationale; operators can override per tenant/workspace; unknown classes degrade to hybrid retrieval with a visible notice. | P0 |

SR-RAG-002.text: | SR-RAG-002 | **GraphRAG patterns:** local (entity-neighborhood + attached documents), global (community-summary map-reduce), path-based, subgraph-as-context, and temporal. | P0 (local) / P1 |

SR-RAG-004.text: | SR-RAG-004 | **Advanced strategies as plugins:** HyDE, query decomposition, step-back, RAG-Fusion, parent-child chunking, sentence-window, self-RAG/corrective-RAG, agentic RAG loops, long-context packing with budget manager. | P1 |

SR-RAG-005.text: | SR-RAG-005 | **Graph-aware chunking:** chunk boundaries follow document structure and link to graph entities; every chunk carries `raw_id`, section path, classification, ontology links. | P0 |

SR-RAG-007.text: | SR-RAG-007 | **Context budget manager:** token-aware assembly, deduplication, evidence prioritization, and per-model context-window adaptation. | P0 |

SR-RAG-009.text: | SR-RAG-009 | **Caching:** semantic and exact caches keyed by tenant, policy version, graph revision and model version; invalidated by revision events. | P1 |

SR-RAG-010.text: | SR-RAG-010 | **RAG evaluation harness** built in: retrieval precision/recall@k, MRR/nDCG, groundedness/faithfulness, citation precision, answer relevance, hallucination rate, latency, token cost; regression gates in CI. | P0 |

SR-NLQ-002.text: | SR-NLQ-002 | **Intelligent suggestion engine (core differentiator):** when a question is ambiguous, under-specified, too broad, or maps to multiple plans, the system MUST present a ranked set of **candidate questions/queries** each with: plain-language paraphrase, the exact QueryPlan/dialect preview, expected result shape, entity bindings (with alternatives), estimated cost/latency, confidence, data-coverage note, and a permission check. The user selects and **fires** one (or edits first). | P

| SR-UX-005 | **NL console:** suggestion cards (SR-NLQ-002), query preview (EOQL + dialect), evidence panel, mode badge (deterministic/narrated/exploratory/report), follow-up chips, investigation canvas that pins entities, paths and findings. | P0 |

SR-NLQ-003.text: | SR-NLQ-003 | **Entity disambiguation UX:** "service account `abc`" resolving to several entities (dev/prod, duplicates across systems) shows candidates with context and lets the user pin one for the session. | P0 |

SR-NLQ-004.text: | SR-NLQ-004 | **Answer modes:** (1) *Deterministic* — computed from the graph, exact, no LLM; (2) *Narrated* — deterministic facts + LLM wording; (3) *Exploratory investigation* — multi-step agent with visible plan and evidence trail; (4) *Report* — long-form, multi-section, charts/tables/citations, exportable. The UI states which mode produced the answer. | P0 |

SR-NLQ-010.text: | SR-NLQ-005 | **Depth bar ("no shortness"):** answers MUST include, as relevant: direct answer, supporting evidence and paths, assumptions, confidence and uncertainty, alternatives considered, recommended next actions, coverage gaps ("sources not ingested that could change this"), and suggested follow-up questions. Minimum answer-quality gates are enforced by the evaluation suite (SR-NLQ-010). | P0 |

| SR-NLQ-010 | **NL evaluation suite:** golden question sets per intent and per industry pack; metrics — intent accuracy, entity-link accuracy, plan validity rate, **execution accuracy** (result-set equality), groundedness, hallucination rate, refusal correctness, clarification precision, latency, tokens. Proposal gates: ≥ 95 % execution accuracy on Tier-1 deterministic intents; ≥ 0.95 groundedness on narrated answers; 0 policy-violating results in the adversarial set. | P0 |

SR-NLQ-005.text: | SR-NLQ-005 | **Depth bar ("no shortness"):** answers MUST include, as relevant: direct answer, supporting evidence and paths, assumptions, confidence and uncertainty, alternatives considered, recommended next actions, coverage gaps ("sources not ingested that could change this"), and suggested follow-up questions. SR-NLQ-006.text: | SR-NLQ-006 | **Explainability (XAI):** "why?" on any result returns the paths/rules/premises; counterfactuals ("what would change the answer?"); confidence decomposition (edge confidence, source freshness, coverage). Do not depend on exposing hidden model chain-of-thought. | P0 |

SR-NLQ-008.text: | SR-NLQ-008 | **Reports:** templates (impact assessment, incident RCA, change-risk review, compliance evidence, executive brief), scheduled/recurring, parameterized, multi-format export (HTML, PDF, DOCX, PPTX, Markdown, JSON), evidence appendix with provenance, approval workflow, white-label styling. | P0 (HTML/MD/PDF) / P1 |

SR-NLQ-011.text: | SR-NLQ-011 | **Safety:** refuse or constrain questions the user is not entitled to; never reveal existence of hidden entities ("redaction notice" lists the *fact* that filters applied, not the content). | P0 |

`Document.description` stores extracted text for Confluence pages and ServiceNow knowledge articles. Attachment records remain metadata-only. Existing HugeGraph deployments append newly required property keys to existing vertex/edge labels during the idempotent schema bootstrap; the bootstrap does not drop labels or properties. This additive ontology vocabulary is versioned as ontology `0.2.0`; the snapshot envelope remains schema `1.0`.

The platform-level unique key is `canonical_id`. A canonical entity ID is derived from a versioned namespace and stable source/business identity. Edge identity is derived from edge semantic type + source/target canonical IDs + source fact identity. Schema bootstrap and mutation code must be idempotent even if HugeGraph's internal ID/index semantics change.

**Problem:** EOIP currently has hardcoded connectors (Jira, Confluence, GitLab, ServiceNow). Every new connector requires a platform team engineering sprint. This is a solution pattern. A product pattern is: third parties build connectors, domain packs, report templates, and AI agents, and the platform earns a revenue share.

**Problem:** Today, one person builds and maintains the enterprise ontology. This creates a bottleneck. In every high-performing organization, the ontology should be a living shared artifact that architects, data stewards, engineers, and compliance officers co-evolve in real time — like a living architecture diagram, not a ticket you raise to an ontologist.
- Share link renders a live read-only view within 2 seconds with no authentication required.
- `eoip migrate plan` detects 100% of breaking schema changes (added required properties, deleted entity types, changed cardinality) before application.

**Problem:** Every enterprise knowledge graph deployment requires weeks of professional services, external consultants, and custom configuration. This is the #1 barrier to adoption. The first enterprise customer who can onboard in under 30 minutes without a services engagement changes the entire market dynamic.

- **Zero-Config Default Profile:** DP-0 profile auto-detects available memory and CPU, chooses appropriate backend tiers, and starts with all safe defaults. No YAML editing required for basic operation.

**Differentiator:** Every enterprise graph platform today requires paid professional services for initial setup. EOIP's wizard enables self-service activation — the key metric for product-led growth at scale.

**Problem:** General-purpose LLMs (GPT-4, Claude, Llama) know nothing about your organization's specific ontology, entity naming conventions, proprietary relationship types, or domain vocabulary. Every query requires prompting the LLM with large context windows that burn tokens and hallucinate. The solution is a small, fine-tuned model that deeply understands YOUR ontology and can answer graph reasoning questions natively.

- **Agent Lineage Tracking:** Every agent action that modifies the graph produces an `AgentAction` provenance node linking the agent, its reasoning chain, the MCP tool calls used, the before/after state, and the human approval (if required).

**Differentiator:** No knowledge graph platform offers quantum-inspired optimization. This makes EOIP the first enterprise platform that can solve NP-hard architectural decisions optimally — a capability that currently requires dedicated optimization platforms costing $500K+/year.

- **5-Dimension Graph Health Score (0–100):** Computed continuously across: (1) Freshness — are all entities within their expected update intervals? (2) Coverage — what fraction of expected entity types and relationships are present? (3) Consistency — are there contradictions, orphaned nodes, or broken edge invariants? (4) Completeness — what fraction of entities have required properties filled? (5) Accuracy — spot-check validation against source systems.

- **Health SLA Alerting:** Define health SLAs per entity type (e.g., "ServiceCatalog entities must be ≤ 24h stale") and receive alerts when SLAs are breached. Integrated with PagerDuty, Slack, and custom webhooks (from MS-KGR-020 streaming).

- **Pattern-Driven Relationship Discovery:** Graph-native link prediction models (GNNs trained on the tenant's own graph structure) suggest new relationship types that should exist based on statistical patterns: "94% of entities of type `Service` that share a `DEPENDS_ON` path of length ≤ 2 also have a `SHARES_INCIDENT_HISTORY` edge — suggesting a new `CO_INCIDENT_RISK` relationship type."

**Problem:** Current EOIP AI uses generic LLMs (general-purpose language models) augmented by graph retrieval. A purpose-built graph foundation model — trained specifically on structural graph reasoning tasks — is 10–100× smaller, 5–50× faster, and more accurate on graph reasoning than general LLMs. EOIP should host and serve graph foundation models as first-class runtime citizens.
